senses.gloss: To settle the result of a game, a contest, or a question.
examples: One goal can *decide* a game like this.
A single vote *decided* the election.
The title was *decided* in overtime.

senses.gloss: To give someone a medal as an official honor for bravery or service.
examples: The Army *decorates* very few soldiers for valor.
He was *decorated* twice for bravery in combat.
The city plans to *decorate* the firefighters who went in first.

senses.gloss: To make a plan, a purpose, or an effort fail.
examples: Driving to the gym *defeats* the purpose of exercising.
The extra fee *defeated* the whole point of the discount.
Bad weather has *defeated* every attempt to reach the summit.

senses.gloss: To compete in order to keep a title or championship you already hold.
examples: He will *defend* his title in Las Vegas this fall.
She *defended* her Olympic gold four years later.
The club is *defending* an unbeaten home record.

senses.gloss: To be the thing that gives someone or something its essential character.
examples: One bad season should not *define* a career.
That summer *defined* their friendship.
She refuses to be *defined* by her illness.

senses.gloss: To clear ice or frost from a car window or from a freezer.
examples: *Defrost* the windshield before you pull out of the driveway.
He *defrosted* the freezer over the weekend.
The rear window is still *defrosting*.

senses.gloss: To be impossible to explain, describe, or believe.
examples: The view from the ridge *defies* description.
His comeback *defied* everyone's predictions.
The test results have *defied* explanation so far.

senses.gloss: To treat someone in a way that takes away their dignity.
examples: Jokes like that *degrade* everyone in the room.
He felt *degraded* by the way the manager spoke to him.
The report describes guards *degrading* prisoners.

senses.gloss: To give a speech, a message, or a formal decision out loud.
examples: She will *deliver* the opening address.
The judge *delivered* the verdict on Friday.
He has *delivered* the same lecture for ten years.

senses.gloss: To help a baby to be born.
examples: A midwife will *deliver* the baby at home.
The same doctor *delivered* both of my children.
He has *delivered* more than a thousand babies.

senses.gloss: To need something as a necessary condition.
examples: This job *demands* patience.
The recipe *demanded* three hours of rising time.
The case has *demanded* months of work.

senses.gloss: To beat an opponent easily and completely.
examples: A team like that can *demolish* us.
We *demolished* them in the second half.
The champion has *demolished* every challenger so far.

senses.gloss: To open out suddenly and go into operation, as an airbag or a parachute does.
senses.ru: срабатывать, сработать (о подушке безопасности); раскрываться, раскрыться (о парашюте)
examples: The airbags *deploy* only in a serious crash.
His parachute *deployed* at two thousand feet.
The side airbag had not *deployed*.

senses.gloss: To press a key, a pedal, or a lever down.
examples: *Depress* the clutch before you shift.
He *depressed* the brake pedal slowly.
Hold the button *depressed* for five seconds.

senses.gloss: To push prices, wages, or activity down to a lower level.
examples: Cheap imports *depress* local wages.
The report *depressed* the stock price.
Higher interest rates have *depressed* home sales.

senses.gloss: To get something such as pleasure or benefit from a source.
examples: She *derives* real satisfaction from teaching.
He *derived* little comfort from the apology.
The town has *derived* most of its income from tourism.

senses.gloss: To come from a particular family or ancestor who lived long ago.
examples: He *descends* from one of the first families in the valley.
They are *descended* from Irish immigrants.
Modern birds *descended* from dinosaurs.

senses.gloss: To beat someone very badly in a game or an argument, in informal speech.
examples: They will *destroy* us if we play like that.
Our team *destroyed* them 42-3.
He got *destroyed* in the debate.

senses.gloss: To clean and polish a car thoroughly, inside and out.
examples: I want to *detail* the car before we sell it.
He *detailed* the truck himself on Saturday.
The van is being *detailed* this afternoon.

senses.gloss: To keep someone from leaving or going on, so that they are late.
examples: I won't *detain* you long.
A long phone call *detained* him at the office.
We were *detained* by traffic and missed the first act.

senses.gloss: To remove a king or queen from power.
examples: The revolution *dethroned* the king in a single week.
A vote in the assembly could *dethrone* the young queen.
The last emperor was *dethroned* in 1912.

senses.gloss: To treat photographic film with chemicals so that the pictures appear.
examples: A few shops still *develop* film.
He *developed* the roll in a darkroom.
The photos are being *developed* now.

senses.gloss: To begin to have an illness, a fault, or a feeling.
senses.ru: заболевать, заболеть; появляться (о симптоме, о неисправности)
examples: Some patients *develop* a rash from this drug.
She *developed* a fever overnight.
The engine has *developed* a strange rattle.

senses.gloss: To read or watch something eagerly and quickly.
examples: He *devours* two or three novels a week.
She *devoured* the whole series in a weekend.
I have *devoured* everything that author has written.

senses.gloss: To take in new information slowly until you understand it.
examples: Give me a minute to *digest* that.
She *digested* the report on the flight home.
The team is still *digesting* the news.

senses.gloss: To weaken the strength or effect of something by spreading it out or adding to it.
examples: Too many exceptions *dilute* the rule.
The new shares *diluted* his stake in the company.
The message has been *diluted* by endless rewrites.

senses.gloss: To tell someone the way to a place.
examples: Could you *direct* me to the train station?
A guard *directed* us to the side entrance.
The app has been *directing* everyone down the same back road.

senses.gloss: To aim words, effort, or attention at a particular target.
examples: Please *direct* your questions to the front desk.
He *directed* his anger at the wrong person.
All the money has been *directed* toward repairs.

senses.gloss: To order someone officially to do something.
examples: Take the medicine as *directed* on the label.
The judge *directed* the jury to ignore the remark.
The board may *direct* the company to reopen the plant.

senses.gloss: To injure someone so badly that they can no longer use part of the body.
examples: A stroke can *disable* a person in minutes.
The accident *disabled* him for life.
He was *disabled* by an injury he got at nineteen.

senses.gloss: To switch off an alarm system, or to make a bomb safe.
examples: You have thirty seconds to *disarm* the alarm.
A robot *disarmed* the device.
The security system had not been *disarmed*.

senses.gloss: To make someone stop feeling angry or suspicious, usually by being charming or honest.
examples: Humor can *disarm* an angry customer.
His apology *disarmed* her completely.
She has a way of *disarming* people who come in ready to fight.
